meta.title: Anafor | Making engineering impact visible
meta.description: Anafor is an engineering intelligence platform. It connects GitHub, Jira, Google Meet and Miro to your company's context and shows, with evidence, how engineering work moves your product and your business.

hero.title: Making engineering impact visible.
hero.subtitle: Anafor interprets the work behind every repository, review and decision. Then it shows, with evidence, how that work moves your product and your business.
hero.insightText: Checkout reliability work reduced payment incidents across two quarters.
hero.visualAlt: A grid of blocks where one opens into the Anafor symbol and reveals a verified insight.

problem.title: You can see the activity. Not the impact.
problem.body: Dashboards count pull requests, deployments and tickets closed. They rarely explain why the work was done, what it changed for the product, or which business objective it served.

voices.quote: Our work is invisible outside the team.
Which technical work moved the roadmap?
What are we getting from our engineering investment?

fragments.label: How Anafor turns fragments from four tools into one understanding
captions: Four tools. Four perspectives on the same initiative, with no visible relationship.
The same concepts show up in different places. Relationships start to emerge.
The Anafor Intelligence Engine interprets those relationships and connects them to your company's context.
One understanding, keeping what was observed apart from what is still inferred.

insight.label: Insight
insight.statement: The payment retries merged this week deliver on the decision to prioritise checkout reliability.

rows.label: Observed
rows.text: PR merged, linked to COM-103 and to the decision recorded in Tuesday's meeting.

rows.label: Inferred
rows.text: Fewer failures at the payment step of the checkout journey.
rows.source: Relationship between the Miro map and the retries

rows.label: Hypothesis
rows.source: To validate with conversion data over the coming weeks

insight.note: What is observed comes from the sources. Inferences and hypotheses stay flagged until data confirms them.

problem.bridge: Each of these fragments means something for the business.

how.title: From fragmented signals to shared understanding.

steps.title: Connect
steps.body: GitHub, Jira, Google Meet and Miro, plus a knowledge base with your company's and products' goals, KPIs, domains and glossary.

steps.title: Correlate
steps.body: Pull requests are linked to tasks, epics and decisions. When there's no explicit key, AI suggests the link and a person confirms it.

steps.title: Interpret
steps.body: Agents read the signals in context and write the narrative. An evidence validator checks traceability, consistency and uncertainty before anything is published.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.body: Daily, weekly and monthly reports, shaped for each audience and permission. Plus an assistant that answers with sources.

how.footer: Agents interpret. A deterministic service publishes.

visuals.narrativeText: Payment retries now recover failed webhooks automatically.

visuals.assistantA: Payment retries shipped behind a flag; rollout is pending.

intelligence.title: Beyond data. Beyond metrics. Intelligence.
intelligence.body: The same checkout story, read as evidence. Three readings of one delivery, and a person confirms the link before it becomes fact.
intelligence.visualLabel: Highlight a capability in the engine

capabilities.name: Fact, then hypothesis
capabilities.body: On the checkout retries, a merged pull request is verified. A link to the incident is inferred until someone confirms it. Fewer tickets stays a hypothesis.

capabilities.name: Engineering, product, business
capabilities.body: COM-103 is one delivery, read three ways: what shipped, what the customer feels, and what the business might gain.

capabilities.name: A person confirms the link
capabilities.body: An inferred relationship is not published as fact. A reviewer confirms it, or it stays a suggestion.

intelligence.closingBody: Not just what was built. Not just how much was delivered. But what it means for the organization.

example.title: One pull request. Three ways to understand it.
example.body: The same checkout work from above: payment retries so a failed webhook recovers on its own. This is how Anafor reads that delivery for engineering, product and leadership.
example.prTitle: Retry failed webhooks so checkout recovers a payment without a manual replay.
example.prLinks: Linked to COM-103 · Epic: Checkout resilience

views.label: Technical view
items: The retry is linked to COM-103.
Checkout recovers the payment without a manual replay.
The change shipped behind the payments flag.
views.source: From the merged pull request and COM-103

views.label: Product view
items: A customer can complete checkout after a webhook fails.
Fewer payments stuck waiting for a manual replay.
views.source: Linked to the Checkout resilience epic. A reviewer has not confirmed this reading.

views.label: Business view
items: More capacity to absorb demand during promotions.
Potential reduction in losses caused by downtime.
views.source: To validate: conversion and incident data from the next promotion

example.note: Potential impact stays a hypothesis until data confirms it. Anafor never presents it as a result.
example.takeaway: Anafor turns a purely technical delivery into something the business can understand, connecting the engineering decision to the value it can create.

states.label: Verified

principles: An inferred link stays a suggestion until someone confirms it.
A merged PR doesn't mean a shipped feature.
Missing confirmation is never a negative conclusion.

demo.label: Assistant demo
demo.title: Anafor assistant
demo.question: What did the payment retries in checkout mean for the business?

answer.text: The merged pull request retries failed webhooks. It is linked to COM-103.
Through the Checkout resilience epic, a customer can finish checkout after a webhook fails. The link to the epic is still awaiting confirmation.
This may reduce checkout abandonment and losses from downtime during promotions. There is no data yet to confirm it, so the next promotion's conversion and incident data should be reviewed.

demo.sources: COM-103 · merged pull request · Checkout resilience epic
demo.permissionsNote: Answer limited to sources you're allowed to see.

trust.title: Your intelligence. Your data. Your control.
trust.body: Intelligence should never come at the expense of confidentiality. Anafor reads intellectual property, architecture decisions and product strategy, so protecting them is part of who we are.

commitments.name: Secure by Design
commitments.body: Encryption in transit and at rest, across storage, communication and backups.

commitments.name: Zero Training Policy
commitments.body: Customer data is never used to train or fine-tune our models or the third-party models the platform uses.

commitments.name: Privacy-Preserving Intelligence
commitments.body: Sensitive information is anonymized, pseudonymized, sanitized and minimized before processing, where technically applicable.

commitments.name: Organizational Isolation
commitments.body: Each organization's information, context and knowledge stay isolated from every other customer.

commitments.name: Data Ownership
commitments.body: You own and control your information, including access, retention and deletion policies.

commitments.name: Intelligence Transparency
commitments.body: Clear about how information is collected, processed, stored and used.

commitments.name: Responsible AI
commitments.body: AI that respects permissions, confidentiality, access limits and your governance.

trust.everyPlan: Security is not a premium feature. Every plan gets the same protection, privacy and confidentiality.
trust.message: We transform your information into intelligence. Never into training data.
trust.messageBody: Our business is the value of the intelligence we deliver, not the data we receive.
items: Permissions are applied before AI sees anything.
Restricted information is excluded without revealing it exists.
